before: Valid stts [1,1,0] media has two-tick mdhd/tkhd/mvhd duration. Both parsers preserve the explicit zero and the malformed-codec control passes. Software packet playback and NativeReader fail at EOF with non-increasing MP4 presentation timestamps: 2 tests pass, 2 fail. After the initial streaming fix, owned decode still refuses invalid video duration; this intermediate failure is retained.
after: 25 integration checks pass, plus 6 root MP4 unit checks and 1 owned presentation-normalization unit: 32 distinct checks. The strengthened 4-test focused rerun passes; no-default-features cargo check passes. No selected checks failed or were ignored.
change: Decode and validate the terminal packet but omit its empty presentation window. Preserve zero in the sample index; do not guess a duration from headers. Both streaming dispatch paths and owned normalization handle the empty endpoint. Seek avoids restarting solely at an empty terminal sample so to/past-end requests retain the last visible picture.
fixture: Owned three-color VP9, durations [1,1,0] at 50Hz, exact analytic YUV16 oracles and an invalid final VP9 marker control. All six fixture/oracle/manifest files regenerate identically offline; no private media, FFmpeg or network.
checks: Both parser wrappers keep raw duration zero.
Two distinct pictures match their exact pixel oracles; terminal empty picture is not emitted.
Native duration 40ms, seek at/beyond EOF, rewind and repeated EOF are correct.
Owned decode publishes exactly two frames with zero errors.

Existing positive-duration composition, hidden-frame, edit, layered seek and I/O regressions pass.
refusal_expectation_update: Per the media regression policy, the private terminal-zero refusal assertion is replaced by explicit empty-window acceptance alongside new end-to-end acceptance tests. Positive numeric clock checks remain exact; non-increasing, overflow and negative-duration refusals are retained, and the corrupt zero-duration packet control is strengthened for both decoders.

sources.note: Sample deltas are explicit nonnegative durations; their sum describes media length. Zero is preserved rather than treated as absent.

scope: One newly supported zero-duration terminal presentation case; renderer, owned decoder, seek and negative-control variants are one improvement.
limitations: Software playback and owned decode were exercised; no physical GPU/NVIDIA claim.
